p: George Place is in the middle of Bathgate, so it's a handy one to pop into while you're in town for shopping or a bite to eat. Bathgate station is on the Airdrie to Bathgate line, with regular trains to both Edinburgh and Glasgow, so you can easily get here without the car.

The town is known as the birthplace of James Young, the chemist who pioneered refining oil from shale, earning him the nickname "Paraffin" Young. If you fancy fresh air, the Bathgate Hills are on the doorstep, with the ancient site at Cairnpapple Hill and Beecraigs Country Park towards Linlithgow.
Remember it's over-18s only, and ID helps if you look under 25.
